To find the stationary points, you first need to find the first derivative of the function, f'(x). Set the derivative equal to zero and solve for x. These solutions are the x-coordinates of the stationary points. To determine if they are maxima or minima, you can use the second derivative test.
replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a technique used to reduce the dimensionality of data. The eigenvectors with the highest eigenvalues are the principal components. You can then project the data onto these components. The mathematics can be complex, but with practice, it becomes more manageable.
